dimensions.definition_quote: Every AICID must be linked to at least one human ORCID.
dimensions.quote: This requirement preserves the principle that a human is ultimately accountable for an AI scientist’s outputs

dimensions.definition_quote: Each AICID must uniquely identify one AI authoring entity.
dimensions.quote: The ultimate authority over the entity’s persistence over time is the human operator.

dimensions.definition_quote: Each AICID record must include structured metadata
value_list_verbatim: the underlying model or system name and version
the identity of the human operator linked to the operator’s own ORCID
dimensions.quote: Each AICID record must include structured metadata: (a) the underlying model or system name and version

dimensions.definition_quote: AICID must integrate with CrossRef, DataCite, and other metadata standards
dimensions.quote: Bibliographic databases can then filter or flag AI-authored works without reading the full text of papers.

dimensions.definition_quote: AICID records must be publicly accessible and queryable.
dimensions.quote: The registry must support both human-readable display and API access for automated systems.

dimensions.definition_quote: At minimum, an AICID record should contain
value_list_verbatim: public references to associated works such as papers, datasets, and software artifacts
dimensions.quote: At minimum, an AICID record should contain: (i) the AICID itself, (ii) an agent name, (iii) an agent type

schemes.empirical_basis: an online survey with published authors

dimensions.quote: The survey was a test of whether authors’ contributions could be classified using a 14-role taxonomy.

schemes.empirical_basis: extracted for the period from January 1, 2018 to June 6, 2023

dimensions.definition_quote: a comprehensive set of predefined roles that extend beyond the conventional notion of authorship
dimensions.locator: Table 1: CRediT criteria based on whether they are sufficient on their own for authorship or not

dimensions.definition_quote: These are publications in which at least one author does not have a substantial contribution to the paper in terms of design, analysis, or writing.

dimensions.definition_quote: publications in which at least one "author" is considered as such solely because they have made a material and/or financial contribution

dimensions.definition_quote: These are publications that have no funding, but at least one author's sole role is to provide funding
